title: Jira AI assistant for sprint changes and release checks
h1: a jira assistant that explains what changed
description: Review Jira sprint scope, reopened issues and release candidates with Dusk Bot. See the exact actions, copy three routines and set limits on issue changes.
answer: a jira assistant can search issues, inspect comments and read changelogs to explain what changed during a sprint. a bot in dusk bot can bring those findings to your chat on a schedule using the ai you already sign in to. keep reviews read only; moving an issue through its workflow or creating new work needs separate permission to make changes.
og_line: read the issue history before the verdict.

app.name: Jira
app.intro: a status label is only the latest state. for a sprint or release review, ask the bot to read the issue and the available history together. the useful output is a list of changes and questions with issue references, not an unsupported judgement about whether a team will finish.

highlight.use: find issues using the project and jql criteria you supply
inspect the current fields of a candidate issue
read issue history when explaining a status or scope change
check the discussion before labelling an issue unresolved
identify the intended sprint for a board review
inspect the project versions before a release check
see the workflow transitions available for a particular issue
apply an agreed workflow transition when the bot has change access

app.setup: connect jira, choose the bot allowed to use it and start with reading. specify the project, board and sprint rather than asking for "our current sprint" without context. give the bot an existing jql filter if that is how your team defines a release or bug queue. have it confirm the issue set before scheduling.

routines_intro: use the same issue selection your team reviews, then ask one question about it. the schedules below gather evidence without moving work, notifying teammates or making promises about a release.

routines.name: sprint scope changes
routines.message: every weekday at 4, review the jira sprint i specified. use issue changelogs to identify recorded scope or status changes since the previous workday. separate additions, removals and unclear history. include issue keys and leave the sprint unchanged.
routines.output: a scope change note for the sprint lead

routines.name: reopened bug review
routines.message: every wednesday at 10, search the jira bug queue with the jql i gave you. read the history and comments for issues that match our reopened-status rule. summarise the recorded reason for reopening and mark missing reasons as questions. do not assign blame or edit tickets.

routines.name: release candidate questions
routines.message: every thursday at 2, review the jira issues selected by our release filter and the relevant project version. list unresolved work against the release checklist i supplied. read issue comments where the status is unclear. do not change versions, statuses or dates.

asks:
a read-only jira bot cannot transition issues, assign work or create tickets. it can still inspect available transitions and bring you a proposal. permission to view a workflow does not include permission to move an issue through it.

issue edits and transitions are not documented as asking first by default. if you enable them, write "ask me before you change anything" into the routine and restrict which actions it may call. connected-app sends have a separate approval setting that asks by default, unless you give a daily allowance. one exception: a bot on **Full access** with no sending rule of its own may send up to 25 a day without asking, so give full-access bots **Ask every time** under sending. that setting is not a replacement for controlling issue changes.
cannot: transition an issue with read-only access, even if it can list the available transitions. a recommendation and a workflow change are separate jobs.
infer a reopening reason that nobody recorded. comments and changelogs can provide evidence; an absent explanation should remain a question.
treat a release filter as proof a release is ready. the routine checks the issues against the checklist you supplied and returns unresolved questions.
inspect sprint changes on schedule while your desktop sleeps. local routines pause when the computer sleeps or dusk bot closes; dusk cloud can keep the review running.

sections.h: use the workflow names your team uses
sections.md:
give the bot your actual status meanings and the jql you want it to start from. teams use different workflows, so "reopened" needs a rule rather than an assumption. inspect a first review against the issue histories before relying on the recurring note.

if implementation evidence also lives in [github](/integrations/github), connect it separately. an issue status alone should not be presented as proof that code shipped.

sections.h: keep the question close to a decision
sections.md: scope changes help a sprint lead plan a conversation. reopening reasons help choose a bug to investigate. release questions help an owner check a candidate. for a team working in [linear](/integrations/linear), use its own issue tools; [product managers](/for/product-managers) can keep the review focused on the decision they need to make.

faq.q: can claude help with jira without changing tickets?
faq.a: yes. a bot in dusk bot can use the listed search and get actions while jira is read only. the three review routines return notes in chat and leave tickets unchanged.

faq.q: will it ask before changing an issue status?
faq.a: do not assume so. keep the bot read only, or explicitly instruct it to ask before changing anything if you allow transitions. the default sending approval is separate from issue edits.

faq.q: what should i give a jira ai agent to start?
faq.a: give it the project and issue selection, ideally your existing jql, plus the question you want answered. for history reviews, define the time window and status rules instead of asking for a general project summary.
